concepts.title: Low Level of Economic Development and National Income Estimation

questions.q: Using the method 'Low Level of Economic Development and National Income Estimation', work with: aggregate_real_output_growth = 15, population_growth = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of per_capita_growth.

Take the relation taught for 'Low Level of Economic Development and National Income Estimation' and work with: aggregate_real_output_growth = 15, population_growth = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of per_capita_growth.
Explain in your own words what 'Low Level of Economic Development and National Income Estimation' refers to.
questions.a: The condition of economic backwardness during British rule characterised by less than two percent annual growth in real output and roughly half a percent annual increase in per capita income.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Low Level of Economic Development and National Income Estimation'.
questions.a: Colonial policies subordinated India's economic growth to serve British industrial requirements.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Low Level of Economic Development and National Income Estimation', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Agricultural Stagnation and Land Settlement Systems

questions.q: Using the method 'Agricultural Stagnation and Land Settlement Systems', work with: total_crop_output = 24, total_cultivated_area = 1200. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of agricultural_productivity.

Take the relation taught for 'Agricultural Stagnation and Land Settlement Systems' and work with: total_crop_output = 60, total_cultivated_area = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of agricultural_productivity.
Explain in your own words what 'Agricultural Stagnation and Land Settlement Systems' refers to.
questions.a: The protracted lack of productivity gains in farming caused by exploitative land revenue arrangements such as the Zamindari system, inadequate irrigation, and forced commercialisation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Agricultural Stagnation and Land Settlement Systems'.
questions.a: Feudal revenue settlements and neglect of agricultural investments caused severe agrarian distress despite high labour dependency.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Agricultural Stagnation and Land Settlement Systems', in plain ASCII form.

Using the method 'De-industrialisation and Decline of Handicrafts', work with: modern_industry_growth = 10, traditional_crafts_displacement = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_industrial_impact.

Take the relation taught for 'De-industrialisation and Decline of Handicrafts' and work with: modern_industry_growth = 12, traditional_crafts_displacement = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_industrial_impact.
Explain in your own words what 'De-industrialisation and Decline of Handicrafts' refers to.
questions.a: The systematic dismantling of India's traditional artisan and handicraft manufacturing without establishing an equivalent modern industrial substitute.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'De-industrialisation and Decline of Handicrafts'.
questions.a: The two-fold colonial motive reduced India to a supplier of raw materials and an importer of British finished consumer goods.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'De-industrialisation and Decline of Handicrafts', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Lopsided Modern Industrial Growth and Capital Goods Deficiency

questions.q: Using the method 'Lopsided Modern Industrial Growth and Capital Goods Deficiency', work with: capital_goods_output = 500, total_manufacturing_output = 30. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of capital_goods_share.

Take the relation taught for 'Lopsided Modern Industrial Growth and Capital Goods Deficiency' and work with: capital_goods_output = 2500, total_manufacturing_output = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of capital_goods_share.
Explain in your own words what 'Lopsided Modern Industrial Growth and Capital Goods Deficiency' refers to.
questions.a: The limited and unbalanced emergence of modern manufacturing, characterised by the absence of heavy machine-producing industries and a confined public sector footprint.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Lopsided Modern Industrial Growth and Capital Goods Deficiency'.
questions.a: Modern industrial progress remained slow, confined mostly to cotton, jute, and rudimentary iron and steel with negligible capital goods production.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Lopsided Modern Industrial Growth and Capital Goods Deficiency', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Colonial Foreign Trade Structure and Direction

questions.q: Using the method 'Colonial Foreign Trade Structure and Direction', work with: value_of_exports = 80000, value_of_imports = 20000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of trade_balance.

Take the relation taught for 'Colonial Foreign Trade Structure and Direction' and work with: value_of_exports = 8000, value_of_imports = 5000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of trade_balance.
Explain in your own words what 'Colonial Foreign Trade Structure and Direction' refers to.
questions.a: The trade regime whereby India served as a net exporter of primary agricultural raw materials and a net importer of British finished manufactured goods under monopolistic colonial control.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Colonial Foreign Trade Structure and Direction'.
questions.a: Discriminatory trade and tariff policies coupled with the opening of the Suez Canal consolidated British monopoly over Indian trade.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Colonial Foreign Trade Structure and Direction', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Export Surplus and the Drain of Wealth

questions.q: Using the method 'Export Surplus and the Drain of Wealth', work with: domestic_capital_inflow = 2500, export_surplus = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of drain_of_wealth.

Take the relation taught for 'Export Surplus and the Drain of Wealth' and work with: domestic_capital_inflow = 20000, export_surplus = 120. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of drain_of_wealth.
Explain in your own words what 'Export Surplus and the Drain of Wealth' refers to.
questions.a: The systematic unrequited outflow of India's economic surplus to Britain without generating any equivalent domestic inflow of precious metals or capital assets.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Export Surplus and the Drain of Wealth'.
questions.a: Export surpluses were diverted to settle administrative costs, finance colonial wars, and pay for invisible services rather than benefiting the domestic economy.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Export Surplus and the Drain of Wealth', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Pre-Independence Occupational Structure and Regional Trends

questions.q: Using the method 'Pre-Independence Occupational Structure and Regional Trends', work with: total_workforce = 30, workforce_in_sector = 240. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of sectoral_workforce_share.

Take the relation taught for 'Pre-Independence Occupational Structure and Regional Trends' and work with: total_workforce = 240, workforce_in_sector = 8. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of sectoral_workforce_share.
Explain in your own words what 'Pre-Independence Occupational Structure and Regional Trends' refers to.
questions.a: The proportional distribution of the active labour force across economic sectors, showing overwhelming dependence on agriculture and notable regional variations.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Pre-Independence Occupational Structure and Regional Trends'.
questions.a: Around 70-75% of the workforce remained tied to agriculture, with manufacturing and services accounting for only 10% and 15-20% respectively.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Pre-Independence Occupational Structure and Regional Trends', in plain ASCII form.

Take the relation taught for 'Infrastructure Development under Colonial Governance' and work with: colonial_resource_drain = 120, economic_integration_gains = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_social_benefit.
Explain in your own words what 'Infrastructure Development under Colonial Governance' refers to.
questions.a: The selective establishment of transport and communication networks primarily designed to facilitate military mobilisation, administrative control, and raw material evacuation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Infrastructure Development under Colonial Governance'.
questions.a: The introduction of railways in 1850 broke geographical barriers but accelerated commercialisation and economic drain.
